title: Midnight softfall warmup notes — evening low-impact rollout
content:
Context:
This is a compact personal scratchpad for doing low-risk releases in the evening window (typically 22:00–02:00 PT). Goal is to move traffic gently while keeping blast radius tiny and visibility high. Use this when: client needs a quick patch deploy, hotfix for a stability regression, or small-model-flip where daytime traffic would be too noisy.

High level approach (softfall):
- Quiet cohort start: small, non-overlapping client cohort (0.5%–2% depending on tenancy). Prefer cohorts with robust telemetry and easy rollback (SDK toggles present).
- Warmup priming: proactively seed caches and KV to reduce cold p99/latency blips.
- Short observation windows: 10–15m checks per step for critical signals, longer for subtle regressions (30–60m).
- Fast escape hatch: clear cancel/rollback command, and on-call engineer ready.

Checklist (order of ops):
1) Preflight (T-60m)
   - Announce in SLACK #release-ops and #oncall with short plan + runbook link.
   - Confirm on-call and backup on-call have accepted (ping them explicitly).
   - Verify alerting and dashboards are unmuted for the window.
   - Validate CD image and SHA: run `redwoodctl image verify --sha <SHA>` (local).
   - Confirm model weights and tokenizer versions pinned in release bundle (model_v=2026-03-08-quant).
   - Run unit smoke locally against staging endpoint (3 prompts) to catch obvious misconfig.

2) Cohort selection (T-45m)
   - Prefer internal test tenants or beta customers who opted-in. If none available, use 1% of anonymous traffic with traffic-sculpting rule to avoid high-risk clients.
   - Keep cohort isolated by route: target specific route or route prefix rather than global switch.

3) Initial rollout (T-30m)
   - Release fraction: start at 0.5% (if single-tenant, use 1 tenant).
   - Warmup actions immediately after enabling:
     * Pre-seed prefix cache for top-10 prompt shapes (script below).
     * Trigger a KV warmup with `redwoodctl warmup --model <id> --shape-file warmup-shapes.json`
   - Document the exact CLI toggle command in Slack channel for audit.

4) Observation checkpoints
   - Check after 10m: p50/p95/p99 latency delta, token error rate (LM faults), server errors (5xx), client-side errors, tail latency > 99.9th percentile.
   - Critical thresholds to fail forward:
     * p99 latency +30% vs baseline AND absolute p99 > 1.5s
     * increase in 5xx by 50% or > 20 events in 10m
     * token error rate > 0.2% sustained for 10m
     * any increase in user-visible rate-limited responses
   - Non-critical but will pause: small regressions in quality or small cost spike. Decide case-by-case.

5) Ramp plan (if green)
   - 0.5% -> 2% (wait 15m) -> 5% (wait 30m) -> 10% (wait 60m) -> 25% then off-peak steady roll.
   - Keep each ramp gated by the same signal checks. Document exact timestamps for each step.

6) Rollback / pinback
   - Immediate pin command: `redwoodctl rollout pin --model <stable-id> --route <route>`
   - If client SDK flip used, send a control push to clients to revert. Include a TTL so clients don't remain pinned forever.
   - Post-rollback actions: run postmortem checklist, gather traces and top failure examples, escalate if >1h outage.

Priming scripts & quick commands (notes to self):
- quick seed for common prompts (pseudo):
  for p in $(cat warmup-shapes.json | jq -r '.[]'); do curl -s -X POST $STAGING/generate -d "{\"prompt\":$p, \"max_tokens\":64}" ; done
- redwoodctl warmup example: `redwoodctl warmup --model model:2026-03-08-quant --shapes warmup-shapes.json --cohort-id softfall-01`
- snapshot a KV key list: `redwoodctl kv list --model model:2026-03-08-quant --prefix user/anchor`

Telemetry to watch (dashboard tile list):
- latency: p50/p95/p99 overall and per-region (especially US-W)
- gateway errors: 4xx vs 5xx breakdown
- LM-specific token errors (decode failures, tokenizer mismatches)
- request rate (rps) and concurrency per instance
- cache hit ratio (prefix cache) and cold-calls percent
- cost burn: tokens/sec and projected hourly cost delta
- quality: eval-set score (if we run synthetic checks) and hallucination heuristics (fuzzy-match alerts)

Signal handling matrix (quick reference):
- If p99 spikes but 5xx stays low: suspect cold cache or KV miss. Action: run targeted warmup, hold ramp.
- If 5xx increases: immediate pinback and rollback.
- If hallucination/faster drop in eval score > threshold: pause rollout, collect example prompts, run diff against last-good model.

Client circuit-breaker notes:
- Encourage clients to keep conservative client-side retries when doing evening warmups.
- Provide temporary header `X-Rollout-Note: softfall-01` so clients can quickly filter logs.
- If client-sdk flag used, set default to `off` and flip for cohort; include server-side fallback to stable model id.

Post-rollout (T+1h, T+24h):
- T+1h: short summary in SLACK: fraction reached, issues observed, immediate actions.
- T+24h: collect metrics, run synthetic evolution tests against production traffic slice, and push a short note in the release log (confluence/linear).

Known friction points / gotchas:
- Tokenization drift: ensure tokenizer version exactly matches model mapping. Last time we had an extra unknown token for a client locale which showed up after 200k tokens.
- Autoscaler cooldowns: evening window sometimes triggers autoscaler scale-downs; make sure instance pool min is set for warmup to avoid extra cold start spikes.
- Region skew: a small cohort can be accidentally routed to a busy region; always check per-region distribution.

Open questions / TODOs (quick):
- Should we standardize a 3-step warmup script and store it in rw-ops repo? (TODO: write PR #628 aims to do this)
- Add a permanent dashboard tile for 'softfall cohort' that auto-populates when toggles are used.
- Verify cost gating: add alert for tokens/sec > baseline*1.5 for first 2hrs post-rollout.

Mini-postmortem template (if rollback triggered):
- Incident start / duration
- Rollout fraction & timestamps
- Root cause hypothesis (hot start? model diff? tokenizer?)
- Actions taken and owner for each action
- Next steps and followup tickets

Notes-to-self: keep the warmup-shapes.json small (~12 shapes), skew towards high-entropy prompts that exercised worst-case decoding paths. When in doubt, slow down. Evening is for low-impact moves, not big bets.

Reference links and quick lookups:
- Linear: LD-3421 (softfall rollout standardization)
- Ops PR: rw-ops#628 (warmup scripts, CLI updates)
- Slack bookmark: pinned msg in #release-ops with sample commands

Owner / point people for this scratch:
- Aisha P. (owner) — runbook and final go/no-go
- Jon E. — priming scripts & CLI ops
- Priya S. — dashboard + alerts verification

End of scratchpad. This is deliberately terse — copy to a proper runbook if we formalize the softfall pattern.
